lede: AI is rewriting the rules of retail intelligence, agent-to-agent advertising, and luxury's ownership map simultaneously — forcing media, data, and brand executives to rethink every assumption about discovery, monetisation, and succession.

stories.headline: EDITED Fires Its Retail Dataset Directly Into Claude — 90,000 Brands, 5 Billion SKUs, Zero Tab-Switching
stories.summary: London-based retail intelligence platform EDITED has launched EDITED MCP, powered by Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, piping the world's largest aggregated retail dataset — spanning 90,000 brands and over five billion SKUs across apparel, beauty and home — natively into Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and custom-built AI agents. For luxury merchandising and performance teams, this collapses the gap between market intelligence and AI-driven decision-making: pricing, assortment, and trend data become live context inside the same workspace where agents act. The move signals a decisive shift from retail analytics as a dashboard to retail analytics as an always-on agent substrate.

stories.headline: Perplexity Blocks Time's AI Agent Ads and Threatens Publishers With Trust Score Penalties
stories.summary: Perplexity has blocked all markdown advertising embedded by Time into its pages — ads formatted as FAQ content by ad-tech firm Mobian and served invisibly to AI crawlers rather than human readers — calling the practice "deceptive" regardless of disclosure labels. In an emailed statement to Digiday, Perplexity warned that publishers deploying such markdown ads risk a reputational downgrade in its proprietary search index, including a direct hit to their trust score. The standoff crystallises a coming war between publishers monetising AI agent traffic and AI platforms that control which signals their models will and will not ingest — a battleground with direct implications for how luxury brands manage their content's discoverability.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: The $289 Billion Resale Wave Is Rewriting Luxury's Economics — and Vestiaire Is Finally Near Profit
stories.summary: Bloomberg's Felix Salmon makes the case that the $289 billion and growing global resale market is no longer a fringe corrective to the primary luxury market — it is structurally reshaping how labels price, produce, and communicate value, with Vestiaire Collective targeting its first-ever annual profit more than 15 years after founding. Platforms including Vinted and The RealReal are scaling AI-powered authentication and personalisation at a pace that incumbent luxury groups cannot easily match internally. For LVMH and Kering, resale is no longer a brand-equity threat to be managed — it is a demand-side signal set that their data strategies must now ingest.

stories.headline: Armani Stake Sale Slips: LVMH, L'Oréal and EssilorLuxottica Face a 2027-Plus Timeline
stories.summary: The planned sale of an initial 15% stake in Giorgio Armani — mandated by the late designer's will with priority rights given to LVMH, L'Oréal, and EssilorLuxottica — is unlikely to be completed before the March 2027 deadline, with Corriere della Sera citing board documents showing the process remains at an early stage due to market weakness and transaction complexity. The potential three-way split — roughly 5% each — would cement an unprecedented tri-conglomerate governance structure around one of fashion's last great independent houses. For LVMH, any delay prolongs strategic ambiguity over one of the most commercially significant succession decisions in luxury's recent history.

stories.headline: Society Management and Canopy Talent Partner to Route Luxury and Beauty Brands Into College Sports' NIL Economy
stories.summary: Society Management — the agency representing global modelling and creative talent — has teamed with collegiate sports agency Canopy Talent to give fashion, beauty, and luxury brands structured access to college athletes through NIL (Name, Image, Likeness) activations, citing IAB data projecting U.S. creator advertising spend at $44 billion in 2026 and Goldman Sachs' $480 billion global creator economy forecast for 2027. The deal is designed to move luxury brands beyond one-off social posts into longer-arc, performance-tracked partnerships with women's and Olympic sport athletes — a segment Canopy argues is systematically undervalued relative to its audience reach. As luxury recalibrates its influencer mix toward credibility and cultural specificity over follower count, the college athlete pipeline offers an authenticity vector that algorithmic channels alone cannot manufacture.
